My own re-run: x-web-lookahead-depth-off, x-web-lookahead-moveidx-off and x-web-lookahead-moveidx-plus-two all KILLED (9/9, 0 errors), i.e. the guard is two-sided. I also independently checked the implementer's `moveCount+1` reasoning rather than accepting it: index.html:713 (and the tableau twin a few lines below) does `moveCount++; setMoves(moveCount); recordHomed();` and recordHomed stamps `moveIdx:moveCount` at index.html:474-475 AFTER the increment; the Swift twin does `moveCount += 1; recordHomed()` (Game.swift:701,710) with recordHomed stamping `moveIdx: moveCount` (Game.swift:457,462) and commit() at :469-470 the same. The projection is correct in both copies — no live scoring bug. I additionally mutated the PRE-check (index.html:696 `moves:moveCount` -> `moves:0`): KILLED by the new `already lost` assertion, so the test constrains both the base and the projection.

findings.claim: extractDecl matched an INDENTED (nested) declaration anywhere in index.html and took the first textual match, so a future local helper with a colliding name would silently swap the code under test.
findings.note: VERIFIED by experiment, not by reading: an indented decoy is now ignored in BOTH orders, a nested-only declaration throws, two flush-left declarations throw with line numbers. I also checked the anchor against the real file — for all 29 NAMES the count of column-0 matches equals the count of matches anywhere in index.html, so nothing currently declared is being missed by the stricter anchor, and no name is declared twice. Column-0 decoys inside a template literal or a /* */ block DO false-positive, but they throw (loud) rather than silently swapping the code under test, which is the safe direction. The `NAMES.map(n => extractDecl(n))` fix at web-extract.mjs:114 is real: point-free would have passed map's index as `src`.

findings.claim: The new whole-body pin covers exactly three functions, but the iOS behaviour it is protecting is computed by their collaborators, which remain substring-pinned and therefore insertion-blind. Splicing `if 1 == 1 { return true }` into endsFirstOK (Daily.swift:128) makes the ends-first objective un-violatable — the iOS tier chip never goes ✗ and auto-play spends a live ends-first tier, bug/WF-4 shipped back — and zeroing liveAttempt's moves (Game.swift:967) makes the iOS moves-family look-ahead never refuse. Both leave the whole suite green.
findings.note: MUTATION-PROVEN this round with my own manifest (0 errors, so the survivals are real applies): y-ios-endsFirstOK-early-true SURVIVED, y-ios-liveAttempt-zero-moves SURVIVED. Cheapest containment without a Swift unit-test target: extend IOS_BODIES to the seven checker helpers plus liveAttempt (they are short and stable) — or accept it explicitly and record which iOS code is text-pinned only. Do NOT chase this with more substring pins; substrings are exactly what both mutants walked through.

findings.claim: The whole-body equality pin fails on edits that cannot change behaviour, so the suite goes red on innocent work and a maintainer will delete or rubber-stamp the pin. Rewriting `let silverWasLive = !objViolated(ch.silver, t)` as `... == false` (Game.swift:684) is behaviour-identical and turns the suite red; the same is true of renaming any local. The pinned text also duplicates the substring pins at ios-parity.test.mjs:160-176, so every legitimate body change now has to be transcribed in two places in one file.
findings.note: PROVEN: mutant y-ios-harmless-rewrite (`!objViolated(...)` -> `objViolated(...) == false`) was KILLED, i.e. a false positive, alongside the two real survivors above. I am NOT asking for the pin to be removed — with no Swift unit-test target it is the only insertion-proof option, and the re-derivation procedure is documented in the header. The cheap part is dropping the now-redundant substring pins at :160-176 for the same three bodies so there is one place to update, not two.

findings.claim: stripSwiftComments ends a `/*` block at the FIRST `*/`, but Swift permits nested block comments; a nested comment inside one of the three pinned bodies leaves `*/` and any braces from the outer comment in the stripped text, so the brace matcher can truncate the body and the pin fails with 'a statement was added, removed or reordered' after a pure comment edit — contradicting the header's promise that comment edits are free.
findings.note: Read, not run — I did not mutate a nested comment into Daily.swift. Same class: the stripper handles only `"` strings, not Swift's `"""` multi-line or `#"raw"#` literals. Cheap fix is a depth counter on `/* */`; only worth doing if the pin stays.
